entries.as: 中国电动汽车极速充电竞赛已进入以秒计时的时代。吉利领克推出的10系列电动汽车首发搭载“金砖”电池，可在4分22秒内将电量从10%充至70%。同时，比亚迪也已推出多款搭载同样具备极致快充能力的“刀片2.0”电池的车型。
entries.b:
| Jul 30 2026 - 7:00 am PT
One of China’s newest EVs is also its fastest-charging, with the ability to fill its battery from 10-70% in 4 minutes and 22 seconds.
But that’s not the only recent announcement of a fast-charging battery that quotes how many seconds it takes to fill up, showing that the race for fast charging has entered a new era which treats seconds as the significant figure, rather than minutes.
Geely subsidiary Lynk & Co. recently
launched its new 10 series EVs
, complete with extreme fast charging speed. The cars are the first to use Geely’s “Golden Brick” battery, with more models coming soon at various Geely brands.
Meanwhile, BYD already has several vehicles out using its “Blade 2.0” battery, which also offers extremely fast charging.
These two batteries are both on the vanguard of a new generation of Chinese EVs that are making charging undeniably quick, at least if the right infrastructure is available.
BYD says its Blade 2.0 can charge from 10-70% in 5 minutes. And Geely one-upped BYD by saying its Golden Brick can charge the same amount in 4 minutes and 22 seconds.
Another major battery manufacturer, CATL, recently
showed off a commercial battery
that can charge at an 8C rate, allowing a 20-80% charge in 6 minutes and 48 seconds. But that’s actually
compared to its recent announcement of a
consumer light-duty battery
that can charge from 10-80% in just 3 minutes and 44 seconds.
CATL’s battery is not yet available in a vehicle, so it isn’t quite apples-to-apples when comparing to the BYD and Geely tech above, both of which are already on the road. But it’s not just a lab test of a cell, it’s a fully formed pack undergoing testing in real fast charging, and it’s from the world’s largest EV battery manufacturer, not
some startup
making stuff up in the hunt for venture capital.
CATL isn’t the only one with fast charging tech waiting in the wings. FAW group
just announced
a battery that can charge from 10-70% in 3 minutes and 41 seconds. That’s a slightly slower rate than CATL’s 10-80% in 3:44, but the difference there is mere seconds.
And so, we get to the point: the common thread among all of these is that each of them mention not just the number of minutes, but the number of
it takes to get a full charge. So China is now working with a different significant figure – seconds, not minutes.
has long felt
that charging times are too long, and that EVs need to charge as fast as gas cars.
Never mind that that isn’t really true in practice – EV owners know that charging at home is even easier than going to gas stations, and on roadtrips, your car will often be ready
, among non-EV owners who are used to the anxiety-causing paradigm of being chained to gas stations, is that EV refueling needs to be substantially similar to the poor experience they’re used to.
There are still benefits. For example, higher power delivery means higher throughput, which means you can get more cars in and out of the same charging spot/station per day, which reduces land use needed. This can be important, particularly in urban environments, especially ones where people don’t have
access to home charging
So, regardless of whether these extremely fast charge times are necessary, the fact of the matter is that they already exist – at least in China.
Meanwhile, in the US, our fastest-charging vehicles have been the
Hyundai/Kia E-GMP cars
, which can charge from 10-80% in around 18 minutes on the right charger. That’s
perfectly fine for roadtrips
, especially since a driver will need to take a break every few hours while driving anyway.
But for people who rely on fast charging for all of their charging needs (seriously, try to
find a way to charge at home
if you can), even 18 minutes of sitting around in your car can feel like a long time. A 3 minute, 41 second charge seems a lot more palatable.
There is one vehicle coming out soon in the US which will be able to charge drastically faster than the E-GMP cars, the
Mercedes AMG GT EV
. That will be capable of about an 11 minute charge from 10-80% on a 600kW charger, which will put it well in the lead… but it’s going to be limited in production and cost well into the six figures. (In contrast, China’s fastest charging cars can be had for well under $30k)
But that one’s still measured in minutes. The difference between 11 minutes and 10 minutes and 30 seconds doesn’t seem like much, but the difference between 4 minutes and 3 minutes and 30 seconds seems a lot more significant. That’s why we didn’t start hearing seconds quoted in charging times until the minutes got down into single digits.
The question of 600kW chargers brings up another point – infrastructure rollout has been far faster inside China than outside it. Infrastructure is one of the major strengths of communist states, after all (for another example, see China’s rapid
high speed rail network rollout
announced its 1,500kW chargers
earlier this year, and soon after, Geely
rolled out 1,500kW chargers of its own
. And then, just yesterday, state-owned Dongfeng
announced its own 1,500kW charger
, and says it’s working on even faster ones.
But it’s not just that the chargers exist, it’s that they’re already being deployed at a large scale. BYD plans to have 20,000 installed by year’s end, with
several thousand
already installed at this point. That sort of fast scaling simply doesn’t happen outside of China.
For example, it took about three years before
the first “true” 500kW V4 Supercharger
showed up in the wild (CEO Elon Musk’s idiotic move to
fire the entire Supercharger team
causing complete chaos with contractors
, couldn’t have helped).
Europe fares better with fast charging than the US, as there are several ~400kW charging units from companies like Alpitronic that are currently in operation, with
600kW stations rolling out this year
But BYD isn’t content to wait in the overseas market, either. Europe recently
got its first BYD flash chargers
, and the company plans to roll out
of them in the next year. Perhaps BYD would roll out its flash charging system here, as it has in Europe, if the market were less hostile. But as of yet, it has no similar plans in the US (though
Canada will get it soon
It’s still rare to find even one or two 350kW chargers at a US charging station, let alone anything quicker.
President Biden’s Inflation Reduction Act and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act built programs to help accelerate the buildout of these chargers. But those programs have
moved slower than they should
, for several reasons both at the state and federal level.
One of those reasons is intentional, held back by the republican party, mostly at the federal level.
reality TV contestant
squatting in the Department of Transportation spent most of last year
illegally trying to pause disbursement of funds
, then being
stopped by court
. In addition, the joint office that Biden created to increase government collaboration and efficiency was
, making DoT and DoE less efficient.
Even after being stopped by court, DoT has
tried to put up more roadblocks
Chinese components (the Biden-era regulation required a 55% US components, rather than 100%).
Not only is this impossible because the US simply doesn’t make all the parts needed for EV chargers, it also restricts America from having access to the best chargers available (as we learned above are being made by Chinese companies), and is done in the context of republicans
shipping EV jobs to China
renaissance in US manufacturing
All of this happened after the party’s candidate
asked for and got bribes from the oil industry
(in his campaign to run for an office he is
Constitutionally barred from holding
), so it’s no wonder why there have been so many attacks on the industry promising
a better future than oil
So, here, in the
land of plenty
, rather than competing to be the best of the best and working to onshore manufacturing of the best products out there, America is
pushing those products away
, and letting the rest of the world enjoy these cool things that we are deprived of (and China is profitinf from providing them to the world).
Instead, we wallow alone in the pollution forced on us as a result of those oil company bribes, subject to the whims of a senile dictator with
no concept of how geopolitics (or anything) works
, losing an industry we could have been a player in, and refusing to join the world in improving the fates of our citizens.

entries.t: HL-3 research towards high-performance plasma and power exhaust solution
entries.c: 零碳产业/能量循环/能源测/发电技术/核电
entries.as: HL-3托amak项目致力于开发高性能等离子体与功率排散解决方案。通过设施升级，辅助加热功率达19.5兆瓦，AI控制系统实现了95.5%的破裂避免率。实验在兆安级等离子体电流下，实现了核心离子温度超10 keV的反应堆级热离子模式，聚变三重积达0.69×10^20 m-3·keV·s，并成功建立具有内部和双输运垒的高归一化贝塔场景，有效解决了边界等离子体兼容性问题。
entries.b: The HL-3 tokamak program addresses critical challenges in developing integrated high-performance scenarios compatible with power exhaust demands for ITER and future reactors. Through systematic facility enhancements including auxiliary heating upgrades to 19.5 MW and AI-enabled control systems achieving 95.5% disruption avoidance, HL-3 finished a new round of exploration and validation for high-performance operation and power exhaust solution. Experiments at mega-ampere plasma currents demonstrated a reactor-relevant hot-ion regime with core ion temperatures exceeding 10 keV and a fusion triple product of 0.69 × 1020 m−3·keV·s. High normalized beta scenarios featuring internal and double transport barriers were successfully established. To address the compatibility of the plasma boundary, various small- or no-edge localized mode (ELM) regimes were achieved, including the enhanced D-alpha H-mode, quiescent H-mode, and the quasi continuous exhaust regime. Investigations into power exhaust integration highlighted the efficacy of advanced divertor configurations, specifically snowflake and tripod geometries, in significantly reducing peak heat fluxes. Active ELM control was demonstrated via resonant magnetic perturbations, lower hybrid waves, and impurity supersonic molecular beam injection, complemented by real-time feedback control of divertor detachment. These developments establish the fundamental physics basis and technical foundations necessary for demonstrating and extrapolating high-performance operations to ITER and next-step devices.

entries.t: 通过内部锂离子转移实现 SOC 失配驱动的颗粒间同步：富镍复合阴极中未被识别的电极紧急降解途径
entries.a: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
entries.c: 零碳产业/能量循环/能量存储/电化学储能/二次电池/锂电池
entries.as: 研究揭示了锂离子电池复合阴极中由非均匀反应动力学引起的长期退化机制。在富镍NCM811双峰模型系统中，颗粒间动力学失配导致了电荷状态（SOC）的不匹配。这种不匹配产生了电化学势梯度，进而驱动了自发的内部锂离子转移，成为电极加速降解的隐蔽途径。
entries.b:
ABSTRACT
                  Non‐uniform reaction dynamics are ubiquitous in composite electrodes of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), yet they are commonly regarded as transient kinetic effects that relax and average out over time, rather than as drivers of long‐term degradation. Here, using a deliberately designed bimodal Ni‐rich NCM811 model system comprising two particle populations with identical chemistry but distinct reaction kinetics—polycrystalline and single‐crystal NCM811—we systematically tune inter‐particle kinetic mismatch at the electrode‐ensemble level. We show that the resulting non‐uniform dynamics generate inter‐particle state‐of‐charge (SOC) mismatch, creating electrochemical potential gradients that drive spontaneous internal Li‐ion transfer—a controlled mechanistic example of electrode‐emergent degradation in a composite cathode. Although this redistribution synchronizes particle SOC across the ensemble, it proceeds through transient internal currents associated with more severe surface degradation, including organic‐rich cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and rock‐salt‐type surface reconstruction. These findings show that collective electrode‐level dynamics can provide an additional degradation contribution beyond material‐intrinsic processes, suggesting that performance decay in kinetically mismatched composite cathodes may be better understood as an emergent consequence of interacting particle populations rather than a simple summation of material‐intrinsic failure modes. Our work highlights the importance of explicitly accounting for reaction heterogeneity and inter‐particle kinetic mismatch in composite electrode design and optimization.

entries.t: Rapid and quantitative measurement of bacteriophage infectivity via fully automated droplet digital PCR
entries.a: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
entries.c: 通用技术/检测和表征/先进科学仪器
entries.as: 研究提出了一种名为dPhaST的全自动微滴数字PCR工作流程，用于快速定量测量噬菌体的感染性。该技术通过靶向保守的16S rRNA区域量化噬菌体诱导的DNA释放，可在3小时内测量多种细菌病原体的裂解活性。在涉及6个物种19个菌株的122种噬菌体-宿主组合测试中，dPhaST与标准斑点测试的一致性达95.9%，并能精准解析常规表型难以区分的微弱裂解活性。
entries.b: The clinical translation of phage therapy for multidrug-resistant infections is constrained by the lack of rapid, standardized therapeutic phage selection. Here, we introduce digital phage susceptibility testing (dPhaST), an automated droplet digital PCR workflow that quantifies phage-induced DNA release as a molecular signature of lysis. By targeting conserved 16S rRNA regions, dPhaST measures lytic activity across diverse bacterial pathogens within 3 h. Across 122 phage–host combinations involving 19 bacterial strains from six species, dPhaST shows 95.9% concordance with spot tests while resolving weak and heterogeneous lytic activities that are not readily distinguished phenotypically. It remains robust during the early infection window despite phage-encoded nuclease activity and tolerates phage cross-contamination better than spot tests. The method captures defense-mediated interactions involving CRISPR–Cas and Sir2-HerA systems. In this work, we show that automated digital quantification enables rapid and mechanistically informative profiling of early phage lytic efficacy across Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens.
